verses.zh: 祸哉，那些在床上图谋罪孽、造作奸恶的！天一发亮，因手有能力就行出来了。
verses.en: Beware wicked schemers,[NOTE:1] those who devise calamity as they lie in bed.[NOTE:2] As soon as morning dawns they carry out their plans,[NOTE:3] because they have the power to do so.
notes: Heb “those who think up evil.”
Heb “upon their beds.”
Heb “at the light of morning they do it.”

verses.zh: 他们贪图田地就占据，贪图房屋便夺取；他们欺压人，霸占房屋和产业。
verses.en: They confiscate the fields they desireand seize the houses they want.[NOTE:1] They defraud people of their homes[NOTE:2] and deprive people of the land they have inherited.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “they desire fields and rob [them], and houses and take [them] away.”
Heb “and they oppress a man and his home.”
Heb “and a man and his inheritance.” The verb עָשַׁק (ʿashaq, “to oppress”; “to wrong”) does double duty in the parallel structure and is understood by ellipsis in the second line.

verses.zh: 所以耶和华如此说：我筹划灾祸降与这族；这祸在你们的颈项上不能解脱；你们也不能昂首而行，因为这时势是恶的。
verses.en: Therefore the Lord says this: “Look, I am devising disaster for this nation![NOTE:1] It will be like a yoke from which you cannot free your neck.[NOTE:2] You will no longer[NOTE:3] walk proudly, for it will be a time of catastrophe.
notes: Heb “clan” or “extended family.”
Heb “from which you will not remove your neck.” The words “It will be like a yoke” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Or “you will not.”

verses.zh: 到那日，必有人向你们提起悲惨的哀歌，讥刺说：我们全然败落了！耶和华将我们的分转归别人，何竟使这分离开我们？他将我们的田地分给悖逆的人。
verses.en: In that day people will sing this taunt song to you—they will mock you with this lament:[NOTE:1] ‘We are completely destroyed;they sell off[NOTE:2] the property of my people.How they remove it from me![NOTE:3] They assign our fields to the conqueror.’”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “one will lament [with] a lamentation [and] say.”tc The form נִהְיָה (nihyah) should be omitted as dittographic (note the preceding וְנָהָה נְהִי venahah nehi).
Or “exchange.” The LXX suggests a reading יִמַּד (yimmad) from מָדַד (madad, “to measure”). In this case one could translate, “the property of my people is measured out [i.e., for resale].”
Heb “how one removes for me.” Apparently the preposition has the nuance “from” here (cf. KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).

The Hebrew term שׁוֹבֵב (shovev, “the one turning back”) elsewhere has the nuance “apostate” (cf. NASB) or “traitor” (cf. NIV). The translation assumes an emendation to שָׁבָה (shavah, “captor”).tn Heb “to the one turning back he assigns our fields.”

verses.zh: 所以在耶和华的会中，你必没有人拈阄拉准绳。
verses.en: Therefore no one will assign you land in the Lord’s community.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “therefore you will not have one who strings out a measuring line by lot in the assembly of the Lord.”sn No one will assign you land in the Lord’s community. When judgment passes and the people are restored to the land, those greedy ones who disregarded the ancient land allotments will not be allowed to participate in the future redistribution of the land.

verses.zh: 他们（或译：假先知）说：你们不可说预言；不可向这些人说预言，不住地羞辱我们。
verses.en: “Don’t preach with such impassioned rhetoric,” they say excitedly.[NOTE:1] “These prophets should not preach of such things;we will not be overtaken by humiliation.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “‘Do not foam at the mouth,’ they foam at the mouth.” The verb נָטַף (nataf) means “to drip.” When used of speech it probably has the nuance “to drivel, to foam at the mouth” (HALOT 694 s.v. נטף). The sinful people tell the Lord’s prophets not to “foam at the mouth,” which probably refers in a derogatory way to their impassioned style of delivery. But the Lord (who is probably still speaking here, see v. 3) sarcastically refers to their impassioned exhortation as “foaming at the mouth.”

Heb “they should not foam at the mouth concerning these things, humiliation will not be removed.”tc If one follows the MT as it stands, it would appear that the Lord here condemns the people for their “foaming at the mouth” and then announces that judgment is inevitable. The present translation assumes that this is a continuation of the quotation of what the people say. In this case the subject of “foam at the mouth” is the Lord’s prophets. In the second line יִסַּג (yissag, a Niphal imperfect from סוּג, sug, “to remove”) is emended to יַסִּגֵנוּ (yassigenu; a Hiphil imperfect from נָסַג/נָשַׂג, nasag/nasag, “to reach; to overtake”).

verses.zh: 雅各家啊，岂可说耶和华的心不忍耐吗（或译：心肠狭窄吗）？这些事是他所行的吗？我―耶和华的言语岂不是与行动正直的人有益吗？
verses.en: Does the family[NOTE:1] of Jacob say,[NOTE:2] “The Lord’s patience[NOTE:3] can’t be exhausted—he would never do such things”?[NOTE:4] To be sure, my commands bring a rewardfor those who obey them,[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “house” (so many English versions); CEV “descendants.’
The MT has אָמוּר (ʾamur), an otherwise unattested passive participle, which is better emended to אָמוֹר (ʾamor), an infinitive absolute functioning as a finite verb (see BDB 55 s.v. אָמַר).
The Hebrew word רוּחַ (ruakh) often means “Spirit” when used of the Lord, but here it seems to have an abstract sense, “patience.” See BDB 925 s.v. 3.d.

Heb “Has the patience of the Lord run short? Or are these his deeds?” The rhetorical questions expect the answer, “No, of course not.” The people contest the prophet’s claims that the Lord’s judgment is falling on the nation.

Heb “Do not my words accomplish good for the one who walks uprightly?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course they do!” The Lord begins his response to the claim of the house of Jacob that they are immune to judgment (see v. 7a). He points out that the godly are indeed rewarded, but then he goes on to show that those in the house of Jacob are not godly and can expect divine judgment, not blessing (vv. 8-11). Some emend “my words” to “his words.” In this case, v. 7b is a continuation of the immediately preceding quotation. The people, thinking they are godly, confidently ask, “Do not his [God’s] words accomplish good for the one who walks uprightly?”

verses.zh: 然而，近来我的民兴起如仇敌，从那些安然经过不愿打仗之人身上剥去外衣。
verses.en: but you rise up as an enemy against my people.[NOTE:1] You steal a robe from a friend,[NOTE:2] from those who pass by peacefully as if returning from a war.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Recently my people rise up as an enemy.” The MT is problematic in light of v. 9, where “my people” are the object of oppression, not the perpetrators of it. The form וְאֶתְמוּל (veʾetmul, “and recently”) is probably the product of fusion and subsequent suppression of an (ע) ʿayin. The translation assumes an emendation to וְאַתֶּם עַל (veʾattem ʿal, “and you against [my people]”). The second person plural pronoun fits well with the second plural verb forms of vv. 8b-10. If this emendation is accepted, then יְקוֹמֵם (yeqomem, the Polel imperfect of קוּם [qum]) should be emended to קָמִים (qamim; a Qal participle from the same root).

Heb “From the front of a garment glory [or perhaps, “a robe”] you strip off,” but this makes little if any sense. The term מִמּוּל (mimmul, “from the front of”) is probably the product of dittography (note the preceding word, which ends in [ם] mem) and subsequent suppression of ע (ʿayin). The translation assumes an emendation to מֵעַל (meʿal, “from upon”). The translation also assumes an emendation of שַׂלְמָה אֶדֶר (salmah ʾeder, “a garment, glory [or robe]”) to שֹׁלְמִים אֲדֶרֶת (sholemim ʾaderet, “[from] a friend the robe [you strip off]”). The MT’s אֶדֶר (ʾeder) is the result of improper division (the article has erroneously been attached to the preceding word) and haplography (of the final tav, which also begins the following word).

Heb “from those passing by peacefully, returnees from war.” Actual refugees, however, are probably not in view. The second line compares those who pass by peacefully with individuals returning from war. The battle is over and they do not expect their own countrymen to attack them.tc The passive participle שׁוּבֵי (shuve) is unattested elsewhere and should be emended to a participle שָׁבִים (shavim).

verses.zh: 你们将我民中的妇人从安乐家中赶出，又将我的荣耀从她们的小孩子尽行夺去。
verses.en: You wrongly evict widows[NOTE:1] among my people from their cherished homes.You defraud their children[NOTE:2] of their prized inheritance.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “women.” This may be a synecdoche of the whole (women) for the part (widows).
Heb “her little children” or “her infants”; ASV, NRSV “young children.”

Heb “from their children you take my glory forever.” The yod (י) ending on הֲדָרִי (hadari) is usually taken as a first person common singular suffix (“my glory”). But it may be the archaic genitive ending (“glory of”) in the construct expression “glory of perpetuity,” that is, “perpetual glory.” In either case, this probably refers to the dignity or honor the Lord bestowed on each Israelite family by giving them a share of his land to be inherited perpetually from one generation to another within each family. The term הָדָר (hadar) may refer to possessions that a person prizes (Lam 1:6).

verses.zh: 你们起来去吧！这不是你们安息之所；因为污秽使人（或译：地）毁灭，而且大大毁灭。
verses.en: But you are the ones who will be forced to leave![NOTE:1] For this land is not secure;[NOTE:2] sin will thoroughly destroy it![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Arise and go!” These imperatives are rhetorical. Those who wrongly drove widows and orphans from their homes and land inheritances will themselves be driven out of the land (cf. Isa 5:8-17). This is an example of poetic justice.
Heb “for this is no resting place.” The Lord speaks to the oppressors.
Heb “uncleanness will destroy, and destruction will be severe.”

verses.zh: 若有人心存虚假，用谎言说：我要向你们预言得清酒和浓酒。那人就必作这民的先知。
verses.en: If a lying windbag should come and say,[NOTE:1] ‘I’ll promise you blessings of wine and beer,’[NOTE:2] he would be just the right preacher for these people![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “if a man, coming [as] wind and falsehood, should lie”; NASB “walking after wind and falsehood”; NIV “a liar and a deceiver.”
Heb “I will foam at the mouth concerning wine and beer.”
Heb “he would be the foamer at the mouth for this people.”

verses.zh: 雅各家啊，我必要聚集你们，必要招聚以色列剩下的人，安置在一处，如波斯拉的羊，又如草场上的羊群；因为人数众多就必大大喧哗。
verses.en: “I will certainly gather all of you, O Jacob,I will certainly assemble those Israelites who remain.[NOTE:1] I will bring them together like sheep in a fold,[NOTE:2] like a flock in the middle of a pasture;[NOTE:3] they will be so numerous that they will make a lot of noise.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the remnant of Israel.”
The MT reads בָּצְרָה (batsrah, “Bozrah”) but the form should be emended to בַּצִּרָה (batsirah, “into the fold”). See D. R. Hillers, Micah (Hermeneia), 38.
The MT reads “its pasture,” but the final vav (ו) belongs with the following verb. See GKC 413 §127.i.

Heb “and they will be noisy [or perhaps, “excited”] from men.” The subject of the third feminine plural verb תְּהִימֶנָה (tehimenah, “they will be noisy”) is probably the feminine singular צֹאן (tsoʾn, “flock”). (For another example of this collective singular noun with a feminine plural verb, see Gen 30:38.) In the construction מֵאָדָם (meʾadam, “from men”) the preposition is probably causal. L. C. Allen translates “bleating in fear of men” (Joel, Obadiah, Jonah, and Micah [NICOT], 300), but it is possible to take the causal sense as “because of the large quantity of men.” In this case the sheep metaphor and the underlying reality are mixed.

verses.zh: 开路的（或译：破城的）在他们前面上去；他们直闯过城门，从城门出去。他们的王在前面行；耶和华引导他们。
verses.en: The one who can break through barriers will lead them out;[NOTE:1] they will break out, pass through the gate, and leave.[NOTE:2] Their king will advance[NOTE:3] before them;the Lord himself will lead them.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the one who breaks through goes up before them.” The verb form is understood as a perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of this coming event.
The “fold” from which the sheep/people break out is probably a reference to their place of exile.tn The three verb forms (a perfect and two preterites with vav [ו] consecutive) indicate certitude.
The verb form (a preterite with vav [ו] consecutive) indicates certitude.
Heb “the Lord [will be] at their head.”
